clue.text: Tommy gets a regular allowance without doing any work for it

definitions.text: a regular allowance without doing any work for it

parts.note: a Tommy is a British private soldier, from Tommy Atkins
what a person gets coming in each year is their earnings or receipts

explanation.surface: A common soldier is handed a steady payment for doing nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tommy is the old nickname for a British private soldier. The definition overlaps the wordplay: money that arrives regularly from investments rather than from a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Unearned money from investments or inheritance arrives steadily without any labour in return.

clue.text: It goes up and down, and round and round

definitions.meaning: a palindrome in a down light reads identically upwards and downwards
something that spins continuously about an axis

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is a cryptic hint: in a down entry the word reads the same going up the grid as going down it.
explanation.definitionFit: A palindromic word reads both ways along the column, and a spinning device turns round and round.

clue.text: Repair a siren

definitions.meaning: to patch or renovate
a seductive woman who lures men

explanation.definitionFit: To vamp is to patch up old things, and a vamp is a femme fatale or seductress.

clue.text: After an examination tucked into a meal with a will

parts.note: an examination is a test
to tuck into food is to eat it, past tense ate

explanation.surface: After sitting an exam, someone eats heartily, having made a will beforehand.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who dies having made a valid legal will is said to die so.

clue.text: Mark how the egocentric journalist introduces himself

parts.note: an egocentric person starts every sentence with I'M, 'I am'
journalists collectively are the press

explanation.surface: A self-important reporter introduces himself by saying who he works for.
explanation.walkthrough: The journalist introduces himself as 'I'm press', the egotist's I'M followed by PRESS for journalism.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave an imprint or stamp on something is to mark it.

clue.text: About fifty join an extended family group

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Around fifty relatives join a big family gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish kinship group sharing descent from a common ancestor forms a large family.

clue.text: Sailor is a good friend to Abraham's nephew

parts.note: a mate is a good friend
Lot is Abraham's nephew in Genesis

explanation.surface: A seaman turns out to be a close companion of a biblical figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Matelot is slang, from French, for a seaman in the navy.

clue.text: Cosmopolitan sophisticate

definitions.meaning: someone at home in any country
a worldly, experienced person

explanation.definitionFit: A worldly person who has travelled widely and knows the ways of society fits both descriptions.

clue.text: Complaint resulting somehow from a nameless germ

indicators.note: somehow says these letters come out in some other arrangement

explanation.surface: An illness is caused by an unidentified microbe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges the thirteen letters of A NAMELESS GERM.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubella is a mild illness, and complaint is a common word for an ailment.

clue.text: On occasions a cross letter is written to a paper

parts.note: the letter T is shaped like a cross
The Times is a newspaper

explanation.surface: Now and then an angry letter gets sent to a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross letter' looks like an angry letter, but it is T, the letter shaped like a cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens sometimes or occasionally happens now and then.

clue.text: Soft childish toy results in childish chatter

parts.note: P is piano, soft in music
a rattle is a baby's toy

explanation.surface: A soft baby toy leads to infant babble.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolish, childlike talk is a stream of babble.

clue.text: He is a bespectacled teetotaller

annotationWithheld.why: He is a bespectacled teetotaller: OTTO is TT inside OO (spectacles), but 'bespectacled' would have to give the OO and be the container indicator at once

clue.text: Afterwards discovered to be dead right

parts.note: the late so-and-so is dead

explanation.surface: Someone is subsequently found to have been completely correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean subsequently, at a time following.

clue.text: Spare the Field Marshal

definitions.meaning: thin, lean
William ..., British Field Marshal of the Burma campaign

explanation.definitionFit: A spare figure is thin, and Viscount Slim was a celebrated British Field Marshal in the Second World War.

clue.text: Thanks to Augustus it's a current asset in Portugal

parts.note: TA is British informal for thank you
Gus is a short form of the name Augustus

explanation.surface: Gratitude to an emperor for a valuable thing in Portugal.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British slang for thanks. 'current' means a flowing stream: the definition is a river, the Iberian river that reaches the sea at Lisbon.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a flowing current, and this one is a major waterway of Portugal.

clue.text: Wait for Jack by the railway

parts.note: a jack tar, or tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: Someone hangs about for a man named Jack beside the tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: To linger or stay in a place is to wait.

clue.text: Traitor sent back twice to the East. What a sauce!

indicators.note: the reversed word is used two times in succession
sent back says the word for traitor is read backwards

parts.note: a rat is a traitor or informer
E is short for east

explanation.surface: A turncoat is deported eastwards twice, prompting an exclamation of cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What a sauce!' reads like an outburst at someone's cheek; only 'sauce' is the definition, and 'What a' is padding for the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartare is a mayonnaise-based condiment with capers and gherkins served with fish.

clue.text: Fight and beat an old Greek

parts.note: to spar is to fight, as in boxing practice
to tan someone's hide is to beat them

explanation.surface: Battle and defeat an ancient Hellenic warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of ancient Sparta was a Hellene of the classical era.

clue.text: Replacing this part of a vehicle can drain one's resources

definitions.meaning: the pipe carrying waste gases from the engine
use up completely

explanation.definitionFit: A car's tailpipe system carries fumes away, and to use up money or energy entirely is to drain it.

clue.text: Henry goes to a shady glade for shelter

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
an arbour is a shady bower of trees or climbing plants

explanation.surface: A man named Henry retreats to a leafy nook for cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A port gives refuge to ships, and as a verb it means to give protection.

clue.text: Shouted to be given medical attention

definitions.meaning: in Australian and British slang, to shout is to buy a round for others
cared for by a doctor

explanation.definitionFit: To shout someone a drink is to pay for it for them, and a patient attended by a doctor has been cared for.

clue.text: Dark-red automobile belongs to me

parts.note: an automobile is a car
something that belongs to me is mine

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that the crimson motor is theirs.
explanation.definitionFit: Carmine is a deep crimson pigment originally made from cochineal.

clue.text: In them students may learn about social divisions

definitions.meaning: groups taught together in school
strata of society such as working or middle

explanation.definitionFit: Pupils are taught in lesson groups, and society is divided into ranks such as upper and working.

clue.text: Furious bombardment of Iran over a protracted period

indicators.note: a bombardment knocks these letters about into a new order

parts.note: an age is a very long period of time

explanation.surface: An angry assault on a Middle Eastern country lasts for years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bombardment of' scrambles IRAN to INAR, followed by AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fuming with anger is beside themselves, livid.

clue.text: Monster held in so great a dread

indicators.note: held in says the answer sits inside the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A beast is regarded with tremendous fear.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-eating giant of fairy tales is a fearsome brute.

clue.text: Lamed in conflict, but got a military decoration

indicators.note: letters in conflict are thrown into disorder, giving a new order

explanation.surface: A soldier crippled in war is awarded an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in conflict' rearranges the letters of LAMED.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallantry award is a metal disc worn on the uniform.

clue.text: The service which attracts a throng of people?

definitions.meaning: the Eucharist in the Catholic church
a large body or crowd

explanation.definitionFit: The Catholic Eucharist is a church rite, and a great crowd forms a large body.

clue.text: Large numbers of them are found in auction-rooms

definitions.meaning: plenty, a great many
items offered for sale one by one at an auction

explanation.definitionFit: A great many things means plenty, and each item knocked down at an auction is numbered for bidding.

clue.text: Made notes on an old piece of Chinese porcelain

definitions.meaning: produced musical notes with the voice
ware from the Song (formerly spelt ...) dynasty

explanation.definitionFit: A singer has vocalised a tune, and wares of the Song dynasty, older spelling Sung, are prized ceramics.

clue.text: Sentry gets instruction to watch it

definitions.meaning: a guard posted to keep watch
a warning shout to be careful

explanation.definitionFit: A guard keeping watch is posted for that duty, and 'be careful!' is shouted as a warning.

clue.text: Serving it at mealtimes may be a Salvation Army custom

parts.note: usage is custom or habitual practice

explanation.surface: Dishing up a particular food at meals may be a tradition of the Sally Army charity.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the food served, 'it'. The Salvation Army is a Christian charity known for soup kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: A banger is a common item put on the plate at breakfast or supper.

clue.text: One who aims to set new fashions

definitions.text: One who aims to set new fashions

parts.words: One who aims to set new fashions
parts.note: reads as a trendsetter, but is literally someone whose job is creating clothes for others to wear

explanation.definitionFit: A couturier creates new styles of clothing, hoping they will catch on as trends.
